versions.notes:
### ✨ New

- improve recovery and account settings

### ⚡ Faster

- reduce manifest reads and guard legacy upgrades

### ✨ New

- highlight new chat and workspace settings

### ✨ New

- prepare experimental release 2.4.9 (#294)

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Context7 no longer asks you to sign in.** It works without an account, so its row in Status now shows as ready instead of "Sign in". If you removed it before, it stays removed.

### ✨ New

- 🌐 **Your agents can look things up online again.** The explorer agent searches the web and reads pages for you, with nothing to set up and no keys to add.
- 📚 **Up-to-date library docs, built in.** Context7 joins your MCP servers, so answers about a framework or library use its current documentation. If you remove it, it stays removed.
- 🧪 **Two new skills:** help with Go tests, and a calmer way to sort a pile of bug reports by their real cause.

### 🧹 Tidied up

- The separate DeepSeek web search package is removed when PiCode updates. It clashed with the new web search, which already searches through DeepSeek, and showed a warning in every chat.

### ✨ New

- **Gentle AI has a page of its own.** In Settings, right under Agents: how your agents talk to you, what they may do without asking, and a new switch that lets them keep long jobs running while you keep chatting. You will find those jobs in Tasks.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Finished background jobs look right again.** When a job ends, the chat shows its card with how it went and its last lines of output, instead of raw text full of odd boxes left by terminal colours.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **pi gets going much sooner.** Opening a window used to get pi ready up to three times over, and the editor froze while it did. Now it gets ready once, and your model list and slash commands show up right away.
- **Updates no longer stop at "Access denied".** When an update installs as you close PiCode, the memory helper now closes first, so the installer can finish.

### ✨ New

- **Automatic really means everything.** PiCode, pi, its packages, the memory engine and your extensions now update on their own, quietly, without a single console window popping up. And never in the middle of an answer.
- **Profiles live with your agents.** Choosing the model each agent works with is now the first tab of *Agents*, right next to your own agents.
- **All your shortcuts at a glance.** The *Keyboard* page lists every shortcut, with a search box to find one fast.
- **More ways to make PiCode comfortable.** *Accessibility* gains underlined links, a thicker cursor, dimmed panels you're not using, smooth scrolling, zoom with the mouse wheel and more.

### 🛠️ Improved

- **Check your memory right where you are.** The check answers on the same page, with a clear verdict and only what needs a look.
- **No dead ends.** Using your own pi is greyed out until there's one on your computer, and it tells you why.
- **Friendlier words.** The usage notice, *Privacy* and *What's New* speak in a warmer tone, in all 13 languages.

### ✨ New

- **A theme gallery you can browse.** Themes have their own page in Settings: every theme as a small window in its own colours, the ones you have and the ones on Open VSX. Hover a theme to see it on the whole editor, click to keep it, and search or show only dark, light or high-contrast themes. A theme from the gallery installs and applies in one click. The gear's *Color Theme* and Ctrl+K Ctrl+T open it.
- **The Editor layout gets the Status panel.** PiCode's panel in the Editor layout now shows the same Status as the Agent layout: environment, MCP servers, changes, tasks, issues and memory, in one place.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Settings speak like the apps you know.** Options read the way other editors name them: *Auto save · After delay*, *Word wrap*, *Reasoning effort · Default*, *Include editor context*.
- **The theme gallery keeps your place** when you show more themes, and leaves out the ones you already have.

### ✨ New

- **One Settings window, like a modern app.** Your preferences, your account and your agent now live in one window, grouped on the left (Preferences, Account, Agent) with a search box on top. Each row says what it does and changes at once.
- **Every button takes you to its page.** Ctrl+, and the gear open General; your avatar opens your account, Sync opens Cloud sync and the usage ring opens Usage limits. If the window is already open, it just turns to that page.
- **Each thing lives in one place.** What Pro brings is on Account › Overview, every update (PiCode, pi, its packages and memory) is on Updates, and the full list of editor settings is still one click away under *All settings*.
- **pi 1.6.** pi moves to its new version, with GPT-6.2 Sol as the default OpenAI and Codex model, a security update and more retries when a connection drops.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **pi tells you what went wrong.** An extension that could not load, or a model a saved chat could not get back, now shows once in the chat instead of silently missing.
- **The thinking picker only offers what your model can do.** Levels a model refuses (GPT-6.2 has no Off or Minimal) are greyed out and say so.
- **Tools lists pi's own tools**, each with a switch that really turns it off.
- **Installing a pi package never hangs** waiting for a password nobody can type.
- **The Agent / Editor switch** at the top no longer has a gap in the middle or a light-blue ring.
- **The Theme choice switches the theme for real**, even when your preferred light or dark theme is not installed, and always shows the one in use.
- **Thinner, theme-coloured scrollbars** in Settings.

### ✨ New

- **You choose whether to help improve PiCode.** The anonymous counts that travel with each update check (PiCode version, system, and whether you used it today, this week or this month) now have their own switch, on by default. Turn it off and update checks carry nothing that can be counted. If you never made a choice, PiCode asks you once.
- **One switch for the agent too.** When pi is installed or updated, it can send its makers an anonymous notice. That notice now follows the same switch: turn it off and pi sends nothing.
- **A Privacy page in Account.** It shows what is sent and what is never included, and has the switch. It also sets how often PiCode looks for updates (automatic, at startup, when you ask, or off) and whether it checks for extension updates. Your code and chats are never collected; they only go to the AI provider you choose.
- **The switch in the setup.** The setup's last step has a *Privacy* card. Whatever you leave there is saved when you finish.

### 🎨 Editor

- **Agent / Editor looks like a switch.** The layout control at the top right is now one rounded track, with the layout in use as a lit thumb.

### 🔒 Privacy

- **Nothing is left pointing at Microsoft.** The editor's old telemetry address now points nowhere, as a second lock. That telemetry was already removed from PiCode.

### ✨ New

- **Agent profiles.** A profile says which model each agent uses, with backup models for when one fails. Create, edit and switch them from *Customization › Gentle AI*.
- **The profile in the chat.** When you have more than one, the chat shows the profile in use; click it to switch, for every new chat or only for this one.
- **A profile per project and per editor profile.** Pin a profile to a project so its new chats start with it, main agent included, and let each editor profile bring its own.
- **Agent or Editor, from the top bar.** The layout button is now a switch at the top right, with the layout in use lit up.
- **Cloud sync lives in Account.** The settings menu and the command palette open a new page that shows where your setup goes, with a switch for every part.
- **Your agents' sync, part by part.** Agents, subagents, skills, agent profiles, MCP servers, models and providers, agent settings and memory notes each have their own switch. MCP servers now travel too.

### 🔒 Security

- **Your provider keys no longer travel to the cloud.** Keys written in full in your providers or MCP servers stay on each computer, and each computer keeps its own when a file comes down. If you used a provider key with an earlier version and cloud sync on, consider changing it with the provider.
- **Update every computer.** A computer still on an older version pauses its cloud sync and asks to update, so it never loses its keys.

### 🧩 Gentle AI

- **gentle-pi 4.9.0.** New chats start with their profile's main model, plus fixes in option questions, fast mode and skill search.

### 🐞 Fixes

- The chat's profile button follows changes made on the profiles page at once.
- The start-up note "started with profile…" no longer shows in every new chat when the profile changes nothing.
- Backup model rows line up, and "Saved" no longer looks like a warning.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **The chat no longer freezes when pi asks you something.** A question or a confirmation that arrived while pi was answering could hang the whole window before the question was even shown. It now appears and waits for your answer.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Usage alerts belong to each window.** Every limit (5-hour, weekly, billing period…) now has its own bell beside it. Set an alert on the weekly window without the 5-hour one going off too, and the cards no longer repeat the same alerts block under every model. The alerts you had are copied to each window of their model.
- **Update all no longer spins its cloud.** While PiCode updates, the button shows a progress spinner, and the memory engine restarts once instead of twice.
- **What's New icons stay still.** The step you pick in a demo kept its icon turning; now only progress spinners turn.

### ✨ New

- **🌿 Each session shows its branch.** In the Agent layout, a session that worked on a branch other than the main one shows it on its row, with the lines it added and removed. Point at it to see the branches it went through and, with GitHub connected (Pro), their pull requests.
- **🧬 Work on a session in its own worktree.** Tick **Worktree** under a new chat: the first message creates a copy of your project on its own branch, named after the message, and the session works there without touching your files. From the session's row you can rename it, review its changes, create a pull request, merge it, or open the copy in a window; archiving it offers to remove the copy.
- **⚡ Several chats answer at the same time**, each with its own questions and changed files. When more than one is answering, Tasks lists each by name, what it is doing and its branch.
- **🚀 A shorter first-run setup.** Five steps instead of seven: the agent and its model are chosen together, themes preview beside the grid, and Escape no longer skips the whole setup.
- **📥 Import is cleaner.** It leaves out memory (every pi shares the same one) and whatever PiCode already has, shows each VS Code extension with its store name and icon, and lists only the settings PiCode understands, named as on the Settings page.
- **What's New has pages for all of this**, with demos you can play, in 13 languages.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **PiCode starts again when you open a folder that holds the app and is not trusted.** Before, the editor turned off every built-in extension, and the chat, Status and sessions stayed empty.
- **Signing in to Atlassian no longer asks you to trust the site**, and connecting Jira asks for every permission once, so the board no longer asks again. If you connected Jira before, connect it once more.

### ⚡ Faster

- **Status opens at once** with its last reading and updates behind it; it reads git, pi and your plan's usage at the same time.

### ✨ New

- **🔔 Alerts for your plan’s limits.** In Usage limits, each model now has its own alerts, like alarms on a phone: add as many as you want, each with its own percentage, and switch one off or remove it whenever you like. A mark on the bars shows where each one will go off.
- Each alert goes off once per window (5-hour, weekly, billing period…) when it reaches its percentage, inside PiCode and also as a system notification when PiCode is in the background. It is ready again when the window drops back or resets.

### ✨ New

- **pi checks your pages on its own.** pi can now use the editor's built-in browser: open a page, read it, click, type and take screenshots, and the screenshots reach the model as images. After changing anything a browser shows, it starts your project if needed, opens the page, tries what it changed and fixes what is off before telling you it is done. Ask it to look at or debug any page, `localhost` included. It follows the editor's own browser setting, not the MCP switch.
- **What's New has a page for it**, with a demo you can play and a button that opens the browser.

### 🛠️ Fixes

- **The plan-limits ring follows the model you pick** in the chat box, instead of the one the conversation started with.

### ✨ New

- **Your plan's limits, beside the chat.** A small ring next to the thinking level fills up as you use your ChatGPT, Claude or NaN plan. It turns orange at 80% and red at 95%; point at it to see each limit and when it resets, click it to open Usage limits. It shows up a couple of seconds after PiCode opens.
- **Provider cards read in full.** Once a provider is connected, its card shows the logo, the full name, its state and buttons with words.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **The memory engine closes with PiCode.** Opening and closing PiCode quickly could leave the memory engine running on its own, keeping files busy and blocking updates. The last window now always stops it, and PiCode does too when it quits; the chats' message helper closes as well.
- **Status is tidier.** The cards line up in rows, the Updates card no longer shows up empty (checking again is a button on its tile), and every colour follows your theme.
- **The update notice speaks your language.** It said "memory engine" in English.

### 🧩 Under the hood

- Gentle AI pieces updated: gentle-pi 4.8.0, gentle-engram 0.8.0 and the memory engine 3.7.2. Your memory is not migrated.

### ✨ New

- 📁 **Your projects beside your sessions.** In the Agent layout, the sessions column now lists the folders of your workspace. Add one with **+** or by dropping folders on the list, hover a project to open a terminal in it or take it out of the workspace, and right-click to show it in the Explorer or copy its path.
- 🔌 **Connect any provider in one click.** Providers is now a gallery of more than forty services with their logos and a search box. Sign in with ChatGPT, Claude or Copilot and your browser finishes the sign-in on its own, or paste a key. If the connection drops halfway, PiCode tries again by itself.

### ✨ New

- 📊 **Context in the Editor layout.** The PiCode panel now opens with Context: how full the chat is and where that room goes, drawn exactly as in the Agent layout's Status. With no chat open it says so.

### 🐛 Fixed

- 🧹 **Compact session is just a button.** The sentence next to it repeated what the button does and looked clickable; it now shows when you point at the button.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Updates install when PiCode restarts again.** The new version was downloaded, but after the restart PiCode kept opening the old one. The helper that lets chats message each other kept your profile busy, so the switch was skipped. PiCode now closes that helper first, and the installer waits up to a minute for your profile to be free.

> If you are on 2.2.0–2.2.2 and stuck, this update installs normally: the fix lives in the new installer.

### ✨ New

- **See where your context goes.** Context in Status shows the share used over the model's window, a bar with one colour per part, and a row for each: messages, project instructions, pi's own instructions, skills, pi tools, MCP tools and the rest. The parts are estimates, marked with ~; the total is pi's own.
- **Room before compacting, and a button.** It says how much fits before the conversation is compacted on its own, and "Compact session" summarises it now. Folded, Context keeps just the share and the bar.
- **A new page in What's New** lets you compact a sample conversation and watch the room come back.

### ✨ New

- **Fold the sections of Status.** Every section title except Environment has an arrow: one click folds it, another opens it.
- **Hide the ones you never use.** Right-click any section title to tick the sections you want to see; the Status tab's menu and the Command Palette offer the same list, and "Show all sections" brings everything back.
- **A new page in What's New** lets you try both on a sample Status.

### ✨ New

- **Every changed file, in one list.** When you review all the changes at once, a list of the files sits beside them, with the lines added and removed, so you can jump straight to one. Turn it on from What's New or with the `multiDiffEditor.experimental.fileList` setting.
- **Hide a folder, keep what you need.** Put `!` in front of a path in the hidden files or search settings to keep it visible, like `"!node_modules/@types": true`.
- **Sign-in windows in front.** When a command in the terminal opens a window, like a sign-in prompt, it now appears in front of PiCode instead of hiding behind it.
- **Every problem in sight.** Up to 5,000 errors and warnings are underlined in a file, ten times more than before, and more of the newest extensions install.
- **What's New shows only this version.** After an update or from Help, the window shows the pages of the version you run; patches of the same version add up.

### 🧠 Memory

- **The memory engine is up to date.** Older memory stores recover better, Windows says what is holding the port when memory cannot start, project names can have spaces, and private notes stay out of the reasons memory keeps.

### ✨ New
- 📥 **Import from pi or VS Code, one item at a time.** Open *Import from Pi or VS Code* from the Command Palette, the setup, or What's New. Pick a source and tick exactly what you want: pi packages, model providers, connections, skills, memory and conversations, or VS Code themes, extensions, settings, keyboard shortcuts and snippets.
- 🛡️ **Yours always wins.** Anything you already have in PiCode is kept and shown as "kept as yours"; logins only travel if you tick them on purpose.
- 🧩 **VS Code extensions install by themselves** from the open registry as soon as you are back in the editor.
- 🎬 **A new page in What's New** lets you try the picker with sample items, and its button opens the real window.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Tomas-Platero/PiCode/commits/v2.0.5-experimental

| File | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| `PiCode-win32-x64-2.0.5-experimental-setup.exe` | install it |
| `PiCode-win32-x64-2.0.5-experimental.zip` | run it in place, without installing |

### ✨ New

- **Conversations whose folder is gone now ask first.** Opening one lets you continue in the folder that is open or copy the conversation into it, instead of carrying on silently.

### 🐛 Fixes

- **The cost in Status counts the cache warm-ups.** What pi spends between turns to keep the prompt cache warm is now added, so the total is no longer too low.

### 🧩 Under the hood

- PiCode carries pi 1.5.2.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **What's New now speaks your language.** The list of fixes is translated into all 13 languages, and the window keeps the news of the 2.0 line together with every fix since, so nothing disappears when you update between fixes.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **The What's New window lists fixes under "Bugs fixed".** When an update only brings fixes, the window still opens and shows them in their own page, and it no longer appears blank when a version has no pages of its own.
- **Updating no longer stops at "Access denied".** The memory engine that PiCode carries is now closed right before the update replaces its folder, so it can no longer keep files open. An engine installed by another program is left alone.

### 🐛 Fixed

- **Connecting Jira no longer depends on your browser.** Some browsers never opened PiCode again after you agreed on Atlassian's page, so the connection never finished. Now a PiCode page shows which account gets the connection, you confirm it there, and the editor notices by itself.

### ⭐ PiCode Pro

- **GitHub and Jira issues in the editor.** See what was reported on the project you have open, right beside your code. Each folder shows its own repository or Jira space.
- **A real Jira board.** The same columns as in Jira: drag cards between them, or open an issue to change its type, priority, people, labels or description. GitHub issues can be edited too.
- **Fix with pi.** One button writes the issue into a new chat for you to review. Nothing is sent until you say so, and a report from outside your team is marked as such.
- **An Account window.** Your plan, cloud sync, connections and Pro features in one place. Choose what syncs, part by part.
- **Your connections are safer.** GitHub and Jira access now stays encrypted on our servers, not on your computer.
- **Buying or cancelling Pro shows up by itself.** PiCode notices the change when you come back to the window, with no need to sign in again.

### ✨ New for everyone

- **What's New you can try.** A window explains each novelty, says if it is free or Pro, and lets you play with a small demo or press the button that does the real thing.
- **A new About window.** Check for updates and get them from there, copy any detail with a click, and find what is hidden behind the mascot.
- **See what the agent is doing.** On longer jobs, Status and Tasks show the plan, how far along it is and what is happening right now.
- **Background jobs in view.** Long commands the agent leaves running appear in Tasks with their output, move to Finished by themselves, and the agent's reply reaches your chat even after its turn was over.
- **Memory filters.** Filter your memories by type, scope and date, and search finds more results per project.
- **A better empty chat.** New chats suggest where to start.

### 🔒 Security

- **Opening a folder no longer runs its code without your permission.** A project's own extensions, packages, settings and MCP servers only load once you trust the folder.
- **Safer sign-in.** A web page can no longer sign the editor in to someone else's account.
- **Signed updates.** PiCode checks that an update notice really comes from PiCode, and ignores it if it doesn't.

### ⚡ Faster

- **Issues don't reload** when you switch between panels: the last list appears at once.
- **A quieter Status column.** It checks for changes less often and doesn't redraw when nothing changed.
- **Lighter background work,** and the session list appears sooner after starting.

### 🐛 Fixed and tidied

- **Going back to the Editor layout** no longer leaves the bottom panel open.
- **The Agent layout always opens on Status,** without an empty gap at the top of it.
- **Updating the memory engine now takes effect:** PiCode offers to restart it, with no need to close every window.
- **Undo these changes** asks first, and says so if they were already undone.
- **Changes** in Status opens and closes its list with the same click, and **Tasks** lists only agents and tasks working for you.
- **The chat's Ask / Allow all picker is gone.** It promised a choice that did not exist: the agent runs its tools without asking. MCP servers connected in the editor keep asking.
- **Show Release Notes is gone** from the Help menu: Show What's New tells you what changed.
